name: Number Reduction
description: You are given a positive integer $$$x$$$. You can apply the following operation to the number: remove one occurrence of any digit in such a way that the resulting number does not contain any leading zeroes and is still a positive integer . For example, $$$10142$$$ can be converted to $$$1142$$$, $$$1042$$$, $$$1012$$$ or $$$1014$$$ (note that $$$0142$$$ is not a valid outcome); $$$10$$$ can be converted to $$$1$$$ (but not to $$$0$$$ since it is not positive). Your task is to find the minimum positive integer that you can obtain from $$$x$$$ if you can apply the aforementioned operation exactly $$$k$$$ times.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le x \lt 10^{500000}$$$). The second line contains a single integer $$$k$$$ ($$$0 \le k \lt |x|$$$), where $$$|x|$$$ is the length of the number $$$x$$$. The sum of $$$|x|$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the minimum positive number that you can obtain from $$$x$$$ if you can apply the operation exactly $$$k$$$ times.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
